newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mobutu, Kabila comfirm for Wednesday Zaire talks.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu, Kabila comfirm for Wednesday Zaire talks.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila confirmed on Tuesday they would meet for a second time aboard a ship off the Congo coast on Wednesday, South African President Nelson Mandela's office said.

Spokesman Joel Netshitenzhe said Deputy President Thabo Mbeki would leave for the Congolese port of Pointe Noire late on Tuesday and Mandela would follow early on Wednesday. "They have a skeleton of the main areas of agreement that are supposed to be ratified tomorrow," he told Reuters.

Netshitenzhe said agreement was reached in mid-afternoon on the framework for an accord that could be confirmed on the ship. "President Mandela and Deputy President Mbeki are both quite optimistic that an agreement can be reached on Wednesday," he said.
Spokesman Ricky Naidoo said Mbeki consulted by telephone with representatives of Kabila and Mobutu and with United Nations and Organisation of African Unity envoys.

He said Mbeki was looking for advance agreement between Mobutu and Kabila on the mechanism for a transition to democracy after 32 years of autocratic rule by Mobutu and a decision on who would lead the process.

"The deputy president is definitely leaving tonight, but he will fly directly to Pointe Noire. He is not going to Lubumbashi or to Kinshasa anymore. Those visits have become unnecessary," he said. Mandela was scheduled to fly from Cape Town at dawn and was due in Pointe Noire at 10 a.m. (0900 GMT).
